name: Four Seasons Rancho Encantado, Santa Fe
insider_take: This adobe-style sanctuary sits on 57 acres in the foothills of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, where ancient Native American trails once wound through piñon and juniper trees.
whats_special: The property was built on a historic ranch that dates back to the 1930s, featuring casitas designed to mirror traditional Pueblo architecture. Each suite offers private terraces with sweeping views of the Jemez Mountains, and the resort maintains four traditional kiva fireplaces throughout the property—a nod to the sacred ceremonial chambers of local Pueblo tribes.
pro_tip: Book a sunset horseback ride through the high desert terrain—the resort's equestrian program uses the same trails that connected ancient trading routes between Pueblo communities over 1,000 years ago.
dont_miss: The resort's location offers direct access to the Dale Ball Trail system, and you're just 10 minutes from the historic Santa Fe Plaza, where the Palace of the Governors (built in 1610) stands as America's oldest continuously occupied public building. The nearby Tesuque Pueblo has been continuously inhabited for over 700 years.
pros: Stunning desert landscape and mountain views in the Sangre de Cristo foothills
World-class spa featuring authentic Native American-inspired treatments
Championship golf course designed by Jack Nicklaus with dramatic terrain
Spacious casitas and suites with private patios and authentic Southwestern décor
cons: Secluded location requires drive to Santa Fe Plaza and downtown attractions
Premium luxury pricing reflects high-end Four Seasons standards
